A layer of your own on a map the pipe makes

Source: R/quick.R
og_add_layer.Rd

og_add_layer() adds an og_layer() to a map the pipe makes (og_map(), with data or none, and the layer functions), for what the layer functions do not draw: elevations as relief and colours ("dem"), contours made in the page ("contour"), tiles of your own ("vector", "grid"), features as GeoJSON with a style of your own. It sits in the sidebar's box section with the others and is drawn in the order added, the later over the earlier, whatever their boxes (or as og_map()'s order says); elevations, contours and a grid go under the base map's labels, as in any map.

Usage

og_add_layer(map, layer, section = "Layers")

Arguments

map

A map the pipe makes: og_map(), with data or none, and any layer functions after it. A map made of og_section()s takes its layers in them instead.

layer

An og_layer(), or a list of them, added in their order.

section

The sidebar's box the layer sits in, by its title, as the layer functions' section; whether it is open when the page opens, by og_map()'s sections.

Value

The map, with the layer.

Details

The first view covers the rows of the map's layer functions; a map with none fits the layers' tiles (their bounds, which og_tiles_dem() and og_tiles_mbtiles() give), unless og_map(view = ) is given. The layer is served, bundled and knitted as the others are; its id must not be another layer's.

See also

og_layer(); og_section() and og_map() for a map whose every layer is an og_layer().

Examples

# the seabed's depth in colour, as tiles made from a grid, under the harbours
# \donttest{
if (requireNamespace("png", quietly = TRUE) && requireNamespace("terra", quietly = TRUE)) {
  depth <- og_layer(
    "depth", "dem", label = "Depth",
    tiles = og_tiles_dem(og_example("dansk_relief"), maxzoom = 6),
    style = list(list(id = "depth-colour", type = "color-relief")),
    colour = list(palette = "seabed", opacity = 75)
  )
  m <- og_map(view = list(bounds = c(2.5, 54.5, 13, 58.5))) |>
    og_add_layer(depth, section = "Sea floor") |>
    og_polygon(og_example("dansk_harbours"), name = "Harbours")
  m
}
#> <og_map> Map
#>   layers: depth (dem), harbours (geojson)
# }
